subject: social-studies
title: Grade 9 Social Studies: United States History and Geography
credit: 1.0 credit — United States History and Geography (Michigan Merit Curriculum social studies requirement)
description: A Michigan-aligned high school United States history and geography course. It begins at USHG Era 6.1, the point at which Grade 8 ends, and continues through Era 9 and current policy debates, using primary and secondary evidence, maps, and argument from evidence.
capstone: A researched United States history argument and policy-debate defense built from primary and secondary evidence with full citation.

subject: social-studies
title: Grade 10 Social Studies: World History and Geography
credit: 1.0 credit — World History and Geography (Michigan Merit Curriculum social studies requirement)
description: A Michigan-aligned high school world history and geography course covering WHG Foundations and Eras 4 through 7, concluding with Contemporary Global Issues. Learners work across scales of time and space using maps, data, and multi-regional sources.
capstone: A world-historical and geographic investigation of a contemporary global issue, defended with maps, data, and cited multi-regional evidence.

subject: social-studies
title: Grade 11 Social Studies: Civics and Economics
credit: 1.0 credit total — 0.5 credit Civics (units 1-5) and 0.5 credit Economics (units 6-9), meeting both Michigan Merit Curriculum social studies components
description: A Michigan-aligned high school course combining civics and economics in one year. Units 1-5 carry the civics half-credit and cover Civics standards C1 through C6. Units 6-9 carry the economics half-credit and cover Economics standards E1 through E4.
capstone: A paired defense: a documented civic action plan for the civics half-credit and an applied economics analysis for the economics half-credit.

subject: social-studies
title: Grade 12 Social Studies: Advanced Civic Inquiry, Research, and Policy Analysis
short_title: Advanced Civic Inquiry, Research, and Policy Analysis
credit: 1.0 elective credit — senior capstone building on, and not repeating, the Michigan Merit Curriculum social studies requirements completed in grades 9-11
description: A senior capstone that raises rigor rather than repeating earlier content. Learners move from studying other people's arguments to producing their own: research design, historiography, advanced source criticism, comparative government, geospatial and quantitative analysis, applied policy and economic analysis, deliberation, and an independently researched, publicly defended civic inquiry.
capstone: An independent senior research argument with a documented civic action and a public or private defense answering unrehearsed questions.
